title: Time-of-Flight Range Equation

c.description: Speed of light (2.998 × 10⁸ m/s in air)

applicability: Fundamental ranging equation. 1 ns timing resolution → 0.15 m range resolution. Modern systems achieve picosecond timing → mm-level range precision. Atmospheric corrections (temperature, pressure, humidity) required for high-precision work.

title: Laser Footprint Diameter
applicability: Beam divergence 0.3 mrad → footprint = 3 cm at 100 m, 30 cm at 1 km. Smaller footprint = better spatial resolution but requires more points for coverage. ALS footprints typically 10–30 cm; TLS: 3–10 mm at working range.

title: ALS Point Density on Ground

S.description: Swath width on ground = 2 × H × tan(θ_max)

applicability: Simplified — assumes uniform distribution. Actual density higher at swath center, lower at edges. Multi-pass overlap increases effective density. Example: PRR=500,000, v=60 m/s, S=500 m → ρ = 17 pts/m².

title: ALS Vertical Accuracy (Empirical RMSE Model)
applicability: Simplified error propagation. Real error budget includes boresight calibration, lever arm, atmospheric refraction, and terrain slope. Typical ALS RMSE_z: 5–15 cm. TLS: 1–5 mm at short range.

title: TLS Registration Error (ICP — Iterative Closest Point)
equation: E_ICP = (1/n) × Σ||p_i - T(q_i)||²   → minimize over transformation T

q_i.description: Corresponding closest points in aligned cloud

applicability: ICP iteratively refines alignment. Converges to local minimum — requires good initial alignment (from targets or manual). Variants: point-to-plane ICP (faster convergence), generalized ICP, RANSAC-based outlier rejection. Typical post-registration RMS: 1–5 mm for well-controlled TLS.

title: Laser Return Intensity — Range Normalization
applicability: Intensity decreases with R² (inverse square law). Normalization removes range dependency, allowing intensity-based material classification. Additional corrections for angle of incidence and atmospheric attenuation may be needed for rigorous analysis.

title: Minimum Detectable Displacement (TLS Monitoring)

σ_ref.description: Registration + measurement uncertainty of reference epoch

σ_comp.description: Registration + measurement uncertainty of comparison epoch

applicability: For cloud-to-cloud comparison (C2C or M3C2). If each epoch has σ = 3 mm, then LoD = ±8.3 mm. Displacements below LoD cannot be reliably distinguished from noise. Improving registration, increasing point density, and spatial averaging all reduce LoD.
source: Lague et al. (2013), Abellán et al. (2014)

title: Scan Overlap Requirement (Multi-Station TLS)
applicability: Minimum overlap for reliable cloud-to-cloud registration. 50%+ overlap recommended for critical applications. Target-based registration requires ≥ 3 common targets visible from adjacent stations. Targets should be distributed in 3D (not coplanar).

title: ALS Swath Width
applicability: Typical half-angle: 15–30°. H = 1000 m, θ = 20° → S = 728 m. Adjacent flight lines overlap 30–60% for uniform coverage. Accuracy degrades at high scan angles; some specifications limit usable scan angle to ±20°.

title: Point Cloud Decimation — Spatial Subsampling
applicability: Spatial subsampling (voxel or minimum-distance) reduces data volume while maintaining spatial uniformity. Critical for manageable file sizes: 10M points at 5 mm spacing covers ~250 m² surface. Choose d_min based on analysis requirements: structural monitoring 5–10 mm, geological mapping 20–50 mm, terrain models 0.5–2 m.
